fields.description:
## The defect

`infra/scripts/install-observability.sh:12` deploys ONLY the probe:

```
install -m 0755 "${SCRIPT_DIR}/observability.sh" /usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh
```

But `observability.sh` resolves its cap scripts as **siblings of its own path** — four of them,
not two (`:458` docker-storage-cap.sh, `:925` journald-cap.sh, `:999` vartmp-cap.sh,
`:1092` container-cap.sh), e.g.

```
DOCKER_CAP_SH="${DOCKER_CAP_SH:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/docker-storage-cap.sh}"
```

So the deployed probe at `/usr/local/bin/rebar-observability.sh` looks for all four in
`/usr/local/bin/`, where the installer never put any of them. The probe reports a value it cannot
actually measure, and the failure presents as a healthy-looking number.

## Consequences, both observed on the live host

**1. Gated percent metrics silently never publish.** `docker_storage_used_percent`,
`docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent`, `journal_used_percent`, `var_tmp_used_percent` and
`container_writable_used_percent` are each gated on a budget read from `--print-env`. With the
cap script unreachable the read fails, so the metric publishes NOTHING — correct
silence-not-zero behaviour firing for an incorrect reason. The caps were installed and readable
ON DISK, just not from where the probe looked.

**2. Ungated heartbeats are pinned at a FALSE 0 — the serious half.** These publish UNGATED, so
an unreachable cap script yields 0 rather than silence. `journal_cap_in_effect`,
`var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active` assert "not in force" **forever, with the
mechanism genuinely in force on the host.** An alarm asserting a false negative indefinitely is
worse than a missing alarm: it trains its reader to ignore it, while the thing it watches is
healthy.

## How it was found

During an operator-authorised cap install on 2026-09-05. Installing both caps was NOT sufficient;
the scripts had to be placed at `/usr/local/bin/` by hand before `docker_storage_used_percent`
(63.0), `docker_buildkit_cache_used_percent` (100.0), `journal_used_percent` (56.0) appeared and
`journal_cap_in_effect` flipped 0 -> 1. `journald-cap.sh` did not exist on the host at all.
Adjacent to `octahedral-auburn-sunfish` (5246-2ec0-1fa6-4637): neither cap script appears in any
of `autodeploy.sh`'s `*_PATHS`, so a commit changing a cap signals nothing.

On 2026-09-06 the same defect was confirmed **still live** for `vartmp-cap.sh` and
`container-cap.sh` (rc 127 on both), and proven independent of host configuration: with both
reaper timers installed and genuinely running (`--check-active` = 1 at their installed paths),
the probe still published `0` for both heartbeats and still omitted both percentages on every
tick after the install. Evidence in the comment folding in `exorable-gemstone-bluefish`
(`1e63-bee1-5ce6-4d8f`, closed as a duplicate of this ticket).

## The constraint that shapes the fix

`docker-storage-cap.sh` and `journald-cap.sh` define no installed path, so their repo basename is
the only name they have and either fix direction works. **`vartmp-cap.sh` and `container-cap.sh`
self-install under a DIFFERENT name** (`VAR_TMP_INSTALLED_PATH` at `vartmp-cap.sh:121`,
`CONTAINER_INSTALLED_PATH` at `container-cap.sh:124`, both `/usr/local/bin/rebar-*-cap.sh`),
because that path is the `ExecStart` of the reaper units they write. Satisfying this by the
installer direction alone would place a SECOND copy under the unprefixed name — the probe reading
one copy while the reaper timer executes the other, free to drift. For those two the resolver
direction is the one that composes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 - A deployed probe can reach **every** cap script it resolves at runtime — all four.
      Either direction is acceptable per script; the invariant is that no `*_CAP_SH` default
      names a path nothing creates. Checked by AC4's deploy-time check.
- [x] AC2 - Defect-seeded: with a cap script absent from the deploy location, a test FAILS.
      Removing it from the installer or from the resolver's candidate list must turn that test
      RED. Checked by `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py -x`.
- [x] AC3 - Every ungated heartbeat distinguishes "not in force" from "could not determine".
      Publishing a confident 0 for an unreadable input is the defect. Covers
      `journal_cap_in_effect`, `var_tmp_cleanup_active` and `container_reaper_active`. Their
      alarms are `treat_missing_data = "breaching"` at 6/6, so silence still pages — it just
      stops asserting a false negative.
- [x] AC4 - A check catches a deployed probe whose resolved dependencies are missing, so this is
      caught at deploy time rather than by an operator noticing absent metrics. Checked by the
      check failing when one cap script is withheld from a rendered install.
- [x] AC5 - For `vartmp-cap.sh` / `container-cap.sh` exactly ONE copy of each remains on the
      host, at the `*_INSTALLED_PATH` their `--install` writes, and the probe resolves it. Test:
      with only `rebar-vartmp-cap.sh` beside the probe, a run publishes `var_tmp_used_percent`
      and `var_tmp_cleanup_active=1`; equivalently for the container pair.
- [x] AC6 - The `*_CAP_SH` environment overrides still take precedence over every candidate, so
      existing tests injecting a stub path are unaffected.
- [x] AC7 - `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_var_tmp.py tests/scripts/test_observability_container_layers.py -x`
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_observability_docker_storage.py tests/scripts/test_observability_journal.py -x`
- `pytest tests/scripts/test_vartmp_cap.py tests/scripts/test_container_cap.py -x`
- `make lint && make typecheck`
- Post-deploy: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace rebar/host --metric-name
  var_tmp_used_percent` returns datapoints and the two heartbeats read 1 on a reaper-active host.

## Non-goals

Not changing what the caps do. Not fixing the autodeploy `*_PATHS` gap
(`octahedral-auburn-sunfish`). Not restarting Docker. Not retuning any alarm: these alarms are
correct, and two are firing on conditions that are true.
